title: Operator cannot pause a running cycle: active:false is silently clobbered by the sidecar's own state write
description:
Found live while trying to halt a non-converging review loop on CAM-358 (2026-07-20).

SYMPTOM. There is no working way for the orchestrator or operator to pause an in-flight cycle short of killing the sidecar process.

OBSERVED, in order:
1. `cam drain --stop` reports 'loop will stop at the next safe cycle boundary'. It is an INTER-CYCLE kill-switch, so a cycle already in flight kept dispatching stories (iteration 9 -> 10, stories 6/10, implementer pane live). The wording reads like it will stop the current run and it does not.
2. Writing `active: false` into .claude/cam-loop.local.md (the flag the loop is documented as gating dispatch on) was SILENTLY OVERWRITTEN back to `active: true` by the sidecar's own next state write. Verified: flipped to false, confirmed on disk, and the file read `active: true` at iteration 11 with 8/10 stories done and dispatch continuing.
3. Only `pkill -f 'cam sidecar'` actually stopped dispatch. Closing the worker pane afterward left a clean tree.

WHY IT MATTERS. The sharp edge is (2): the flag LOOKS like it worked. The file accepts the write, nothing warns, and the loop keeps spending tokens and committing to the branch. An operator watching a loop go wrong has no graceful brake, and the only working stop is a hammer that also destroys the sidecar's in-memory state (merge-watch timers, which per the recovery runbook then require driving post-merge by hand).

SCOPE TO CONSIDER.
- Make `active: false` authoritative: the loop should observe it and halt at the next story boundary rather than round-tripping its own cached state over it. Whatever the current write ordering is, an external flip must win.
- Either give `cam drain` an intra-cycle mode or correct its output text so it cannot be read as stopping the current run.
- Consider a first-class `cam pause` / `cam resume` that halts at the next story boundary, leaves the sidecar and its in-memory watches alive, and is visible in `cam status`.
- `cam stop` exists but is documented as killing the per-project tmux session, which would take the orchestrator's own pane down with it; that is not a usable brake from inside the session.

EVIDENCE. Session of 2026-07-20, branch cam/issue-358, sidecar pid 38167 at 0.216.0.

spec.scope: Add a first-class cam pause / cam resume operator brake that halts an in-flight autonomous implement cycle at the next story boundary, leaving the sidecar process and its in-memory merge-watch timers alive, and surfaces a distinct operator-initiated paused state in cam status. The pause signal is a dedicated marker file under .claude, NOT the loop-state active field (which is phase-derived and re-stamped active:true every iteration by makeOnProgress). The supervisor inner story loop gains an injected pause predicate consulted at the story boundary before dispatching the next story; when paused it stops dispatching without tearing down the sidecar process, and cam resume clears the marker so the cycle continues the remaining unpassed stories.
acceptanceCriteria: cam pause writes a dedicated pause marker file and cam resume removes it, independent of the loop-state active/phase field. [oracle: bun test test/commands/pause.test.ts]

The supervisor inner story loop does not dispatch the next story when the pause marker is set, via an injected pause predicate consulted at the story boundary. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/pause-halt.test.ts]
Pausing leaves the sidecar process and its in-memory merge-watch timers alive, distinct from the cam stop teardown. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
cam status renders a distinct operator-initiated paused state, not conflated with the non-implementing phases. [oracle: bun test test/commands/status-paused.test.ts]
cam resume clears the marker and the cycle continues the remaining unpassed stories. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/pause-resume.test.ts]
The full quality spine passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: active is phase-derived: parseStateFile (src/commands/status.ts:262-270) sets active = (phase === 'implementing') and ignores a raw active field whenever a phase key is present, so a hand-written active:false is a dead letter. Do NOT reuse the active field for pause; use a dedicated marker file.

The clobber: makeOnProgress (src/supervisor/host.ts:389-399) re-renders the loop-state file with active:true every inner-loop iteration and is not read-modify-write, so any flag written into the state file is overwritten each story. The pause marker must be a separate file that this writer never touches.

No cooperative halt exists inside runSupervisor: the inner loop 'outer: while' at src/supervisor/loop.ts:953 runs straight to a terminal SupervisorResult. Add an injected pause predicate on RunSupervisorOptions (options bag near loop.ts:330-530), consulted at the loop top (loop.ts:953). The outer loop readActive gate (loop.ts:2245-2301) is inter-cycle only and cannot interrupt an in-flight runSupervisor.

Keep the sidecar process and merge-watch timers alive: pause must NOT tear down the process. That is cam stop (src/commands/stop.ts), which kills the -L cam tmux session and would take the orchestrator's own pane down with it. Halt cooperatively and idle; never exit the sidecar to pause.

cam status conflation: parseStateFile and renderStateIndicator render every non-implementing phase (idle, planning, shipping, awaiting-operator) as paused/active:false (status.ts:460, 511-513, 601-602). The new operator-paused state must be read from the pause marker and rendered distinctly, not folded into that existing label.

Sidecar-executed rebuild required: src/supervisor/loop.ts, src/supervisor/host.ts and src/commands/sidecar.ts are executed by the running sidecar, so after ship do the coherence rebuild (bash scripts/build-release.sh --install, then restart cam sidecar).
cam resume continues, does not re-plan: re-entering runSupervisor re-reads prd.json and dispatches the next unpassed story, so resume is clear-marker-and-proceed, never a fresh plan.
